cohort: The study involved 60 non-pregnant women with a history of Cesarean section (CS) but without any known systemic cause.
finding: Saline-infused sonohysterography (SISH) was found to be a superior tool for assessing uterine niches in non-pregnant women with a history of CS compared to transvaginal ultrasound (TVU), revealing significantly higher niche dimensions.
mod_finding: The number of previous Cesarean sections was significantly associated with the rate of CS niche detection, which increased with an increasing number of previous CSs.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken at a single point in time in non-pregnant women with a history of Cesarean sections, with the specific interval post-CS not provided.
